comments.text:
As a Taiwanese person, during my six-month business trip to the US, I grew to really love the country, but I also realized how completely puzzled I was by it. In America, having a car is celebrated as "freedom." But when you’re forced to pay $1,000 a month on car loans, insurance, and gas just to buy groceries or get to work, it feels less like freedom and more like a mandatory subscription fee just to exist in society.

     In Taiwan, robust public infrastructure covers that basic need so mobility doesn't come with a heavy financial price tag. This makes me wonder: Could Elon Musk’s push for autonomous vehicles actually be an attempt to fix this American dilemma? If self-driving tech succeeds and removes the burden of car ownership, isn't he effectively delivering a new kind of true freedom for everyone?
